SystemSketch · 2026-09-03

Sharpening the chrome

Thirty UI/UX defects found by driving the running product in a real browser, not by reading the source. Ten fixed, each proved in the app it changed. Every number on this page is measured at build time from this tree and from the journey's own JSON.

30 candidates, all measured live 10 shipped 19/19 browser checks tsc + vitest + python green 37 files changed, 2346 insertions(+), 917 deletions(-) window.confirm call sites: 0

Before and after, in the running app

Left is main, captured from a throwaway copy of that commit; right is this branch. Same seeded board, same window, same gestures.

The ten changes

Ordered as they were prioritised: the systematic keyboard gap first, then the dead ends a user actually walks into, then friction, then polish.

1

One focus ring for every surface the app owns

A real Tab into the palette left outline: none on the focused control; five stylesheets had zero :focus-visible rules between them. The ring now lives once, in app.css, scoped to app-owned roots so tldraw's own focus treatment is left alone, with an inset variant for the inverse pill and its dark palettes. One deliberate exception, from review: a palette tab takes no ring. Selection follows focus there, so the focused tab is always the selected tab and a ring would be a second mark for a fact the raised chip already carries. Every control where focus and selection differ keeps its ring, and the journey asserts both halves.

src/app.css
2

The dock always has a header you can close it with

block-inspector.css hid the frame's header for every inspector subject, and a second rule in systemsketch-chrome.css keyed on .block-inspector__header, a class that exists nowhere in src. A cable, an ordinary shape and an empty selection each got a headerless column with no pointer way out. One attribute rule now replaces both, driven by inspectorSubjectOwnsHeader.

src/chrome/inspectorSubject.ts
3

The dock follows the selection; Inspect is gone

The pill offered Inspect for every selection, and a rectangle that took the offer landed on “Select a Block to inspect it.” — an action whose only outcome was a contradiction of itself. Review found the button itself was the redundancy: it only ever meant “show me the panel for what I already selected”, a step the selection had taken. So the button is gone from both pills and the dock follows every selection, an ordinary shape included — where it now states what tldraw already holds, inventing no semantics a whiteboard does not have. Show inspector in the command palette is the one deliberate way back to a dock you dismissed without changing the selection.

src/chrome/shapeFactsModel.ts
4

An explicit dismissal of the dock is respected, and Escape stays on the canvas

Measured: the dock auto-opened, the user closed it, and selecting a second Block re-opened it. The close is now remembered against the context it was made on and released when the selection empties, so it sticks for that run of selections and never becomes permanent. A dock that follows the selection is also open most of the time, which made a second rule necessary: Escape no longer closes it. Drawing a rectangle selects it and opens the dock, so the Escape meant to return the geo tool to select was closing the panel instead — leaving the tool armed with no selection pill. Escape closes the surfaces a person opened; the dock closes with its own × or by clearing the selection.

src/chrome/ChromeProvider.tsx
5

One app-owned confirm replaces both native ones

Deleting a comment thread and moving a board to Trash asked with window.confirm: an OS modal that steals focus from a canvas mid-gesture, cannot wear the board's theme, and may be suppressed outright inside a VS Code or Obsidian webview. The ask now goes through tldraw's own dialog stack and returns a promise, so each call site reads as it did.

src/chrome/ConfirmDialog.tsx
6

The Block view switcher explains itself

The pill shows one capital per view because three names would be wider than the pill — but measured, S, P and E carried title: null, so hovering taught nothing and only a screen reader ever heard the label. Inspect had neither. All four now carry a tooltip and a name.

src/blocks/ui/BlockSelectionMiniMenu.tsx
7

Three malformed ARIA widgets, made real

The palette's mode switch had two role="tab" buttons both at tabIndex=0, no aria-controls, no tabpanel and no arrow keys; 28 menuitemradio options sat in a group with no menu ancestor; the theme radiogroup ignored the arrows. Each is now the widget it claimed to be, one tab stop with arrow-key navigation.

src/commands/SystemSketchCommandPalette.tsx
8

The appearance palette keeps clear of the window edge

Measured at a 520px window: the 455px colour panel opened at x=0, its first swatch column cut in half, because the two appearance popovers were the only ones in the app not passing a collision padding. They now keep the same 12px as everything else.

src/appearance/figjamTokens.ts
9

Thin themed scrollbars in every app panel

Every panel scrolls its own body, and each drew the OS scrollbar — a wide grey trough against an 18px-radius designed panel. Both the Firefox and the WebKit/Blink spellings are declared rather than one being assumed.

src/app.css
10

The profile badge does the thing its shape promises

The Z badge was a button titled “Profile placeholder” that did nothing when pressed. There is no identity to show — SystemSketch is local and single-user — so it now opens the preferences a profile badge implies: the same Settings dialog the main menu opens, landing on the theme panel.

src/chrome/SystemSketchChrome.tsx

What the browser measured

npm run test:ui-hardening — 717 lines driving real Chrome against the real product profile, with zero local console errors.

  • every app panel paints a thin themed scrollbar instead of the OS one
  • the palette mode switch is one tab stop that controls a real tabpanel
  • the palette tablist says which tab is on through one mark, not a ring competing with a chip
  • arrow keys walk the palette tablist and selection follows focus
  • every palette control that is not a tab still paints a ring
  • selecting an ordinary shape opens its real facts panel, with no Inspect button in the pill
  • the facts panel Fit to view action really moves the camera
  • the dock header close button closes a headerless-subject panel
  • closing the dock sticks for that run of selections and releases on an empty selection
  • Escape returns the tool to select rather than being swallowed by the dock
  • every Block mini-menu control carries a tooltip and an accessible name
  • the appearance palette keeps the app-wide 12px clear of the window edge
  • a keyboard-focused appearance swatch paints a ring on the inverse panel
  • the profile badge opens the real Settings dialog on the theme panel
  • the theme radiogroup is one tab stop the arrow keys operate
  • an unbuilt Settings category is reachable, announced, visibly explained, and inert
  • a keyboard-focused comments control paints a visible ring
  • destructive actions ask through the app dialog, cancel safely, and really delete
  • the physical journey produced zero local console errors

Deliberately not taken. The 8px uppercase eyebrows would move geometry that several browser journeys assert; the system-dark token contradiction is only reachable for a theme with no block of its own; and the remaining follow-ups are real but small. Each is listed above rather than quietly dropped.
